Fields and rules by entity:
- **tag** - 2-1 the tag (required, at most 63 characters), 2-3 description (at most 250); rec_OwnerUGrpID

- **bookmark** - 2-13 the record (required, visible to the user, not changed later), Rating 2-1190 (0-5),
  2-4 notes, PrivateInfo 2-1192 (at most 140 characters, stored encrypted with the key of the installation;
  without a key as text, with the warning not_encrypted in meta.issues). The owner is always the user; only
  the user reads and changes their bookmarks. One bookmark per record and user (409 duplicate, existing).

- **reminder** - 2-13 the record (required); exactly one recipient - Recipient 2-1193 (a user or a group)
  or 2-23 (e-mail addresses, comma separated); 2-4 message (at most 1000 characters); 2-10 start date
  YYYY-MM-DD (today by default); Frequency 2-1191 (a term of 2-10454, once by default).

- **user** (administrators only) - record type System user 2-1107; the fields are named by DT_* constants
  on the server (UserGroupCodes). A login name, an e-mail and a password are required; the password is
  written only (hashed as legacy) and never given back.

- **group** (any user, who becomes its admin) - record type System User Group 2-1108. A unique name is
  required; the members (relmarker DT_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP 2-1200, the role as relation type) are written by

- **website** (99-51) - the server adds the starter header, home content, footer and configuration, makes it

- **page** (99-52) - public unless the body says otherwise.
- **report** (2-1104) - the file name (2-62) is set here and does not change later. It has only letters, digits, spaces
  and - _ ( ) . , @, and starts with a letter, a digit or "(" (422 otherwise); empty is made from the title; a new record gets an empty file or
  takes a file without a record (registration).

- **output** (2-1105, a generated report) - the query (2-12) may not have parameters $X$ (422); its file is

description: Logically DELETE followed by POST in one transaction, after complete validation. Requires UPDATE_MAIL when recognized mail configuration exists, otherwise CREATE_MAIL. Does not require DELETE_MAIL or generic RR permissions. The zone's existence alone does not make a configuration an update. Permissions and ownership are checked on every affected name. Omitted policy sections use creation defaults; omitted/empty DKIM removes obsolete recognized selectors. Keep old selectors in the request during key rotation while signed messages remain in transit. CNAME and delegated DKIM subtrees are preserved; unsafe replacements conflict. Unrelated RRs always survive. Omitted address fields preserve addresses of retained MX hosts; obsolete dedicated addresses are removed only with validated exclusive ownership. Addresses created by provisioning can be updated while exclusive; manually created, modified, or shared addresses require the generic RR API for changes. Identical PUT makes no DNS writes, serial increments, notifications, or retry-budget resets. MTA-STS downgrades, removal, or incompatible enforced MX changes follow RFC 8461 retirement: atomically publish mode none and a new TXT ID, retain the current mail configuration, and schedule final replacement after all possibly cached policies expire, including older policies with longer max_age. Return status pending, transition ID, applied policy and earliest_completion (UTC Unix seconds). Poll GET /provision/mail/{domain}/status. A newer request atomically supersedes pending work; repeated identical requests reuse it, including terminal failures. Deferred work rechecks the initiating principal, ownership and DNS; unsafe manual edits fail without deleting them. Persisted retries default to five after the first attempt; timed_task_max_retries and timed_task_concurrency (default 8) are server variables. Limits and validation are the same as POST. Tenant impersonation is unsupported.

Extend the signatures of a PDF
description: Extends every signature of a PDF to PAdES-BASELINE-T, -LT or -LTA. The result is the input PDF followed by an incremental update, so the original signatures stay valid. LT embeds the certificates and revocation data the signatures need; T and LTA add a document timestamp from the server's TSA. A B-level signature extended to LT needs the TSA too: it gets a timestamp first. DSS checks the signatures first and refuses with `EXTENSION_FAILED` when one does not validate, a certificate is revoked or expired, revocation data is missing, every signature is already at a higher level than the target, or a timestamp is needed and no TSA is configured; a TSA that cannot be reached or answers badly is `TSA_FAILED`. Known DSS issue: on a PDF with a signed field whose `/Lock` restricts all fields (FieldMDP `Action=All`), DSS 6.5.1 reports the document timestamp its own LTA extension adds as a change the lock forbids (a `FieldMDP` / `SigFieldLock` warning when the result is validated); the verdict is unaffected.

Writes up to `maxBatchItems` records, each with optimistic concurrency: an item is written
only if `baseVersion` names the record's version on the server, or is null and the record
doesn't exist yet. Items are written independently and answered in order, one result each,
so one rejected item doesn't fail the others. Each id appears at most once.

**A conflict is a merge instruction.** A `409` item carries the server's current record.
The client unseals it, merges, and pushes again with the current version.

**A delete is a tombstone.** An item with `deleted: true` keeps the record's row, drops its
ciphertext and sets `deletedAt`, so other devices learn of the delete on their next pull.
It also deletes the record's blobs. Writing a record again over its tombstone, by naming
the tombstone's version, is how a merge brings back a record deleted on another device.

description: Create page

In order to upload a media (video, image, audio) or text file, you can request for a signed URL from the API.

You must pass in the name of the file that you wish to upload, along with the file size in the request body. Additionally you can pass "showAudioResult" to select if the audio for a video being uploaded should also be \*evaluated.

Once you have the signed URL, you can use it to PUT the file to Reality Defender (bearer token is not required for the PUT).

The following formats are supported:

- Video → .mp4, .mov (max size 100 MB)
- Image → .jpg, .png, .jpeg, .gif, .webp (max size 10 MB)
- Audio → .flac, .wav, .mp3, .m4a, .aac, .ogg (max size 20 MB)
- Text → .txt (max size 5 MB with every 2000 characters considered as one scan)
    

\*Note: If you wish to evaluate the audio track from a video, our system will do this automatically (the feature must be enabled for your account). If you run the audio extraction yourself and upload the audio file separately, it may result in data loss and reduce the accuracy of the Audio models.
